<reason>Both sides argued the motion as written and clashed cleanly, but CON built the more decisive decision route. CON's central dilemma — who actually performs the "refusal"? — was pressed from the opening through the closing and never fully resolved. PRO's answer (a platform-run "threshold review" that gates only whether the rating may drive consequences) was a genuine attempt to split the horns, and the distinction between a proportionality appeal and an instrument-validity review was PRO's best original move. But CON's rejoinder landed hard: PRO spends the debate indicting platform bad faith and then hands the platform the gavel, while CON's code-level remedies (outlier discard, peer benchmarking, stripping rating rights from customers whose scores track accents and names) are publicly auditable under the same compulsion lever. PRO's counter that a single adjudication is court-auditable was reasonable but thinner than CON's "publish the distribution" answer. On safety, PRO's sharpest hit — that CON's own demand for investigation concedes ratings cannot be trusted to act directly — was answered well by the tripwire/response distinction (the star is cheap and universally given, complaints are high-friction and non-comparable), and PRO's closing merely re-asserted the concession claim without engaging that distinction. CON also converted PRO's two pressure answers into a live bind (refusal that changes nothing, or concealment that hides the absence of measurement from customers), which PRO declared false but did not dissolve. PRO's moral framing was vivid and its rhetoric strong; CON's was equally crisp while doing more comparative work. Minor grounding cost to PRO for citing a nonexistent reference id and for slightly confident claims about platform data releases.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's [B2.1]-[B2.3] and its closing restatement: forcing PRO to specify who adjudicates "strongly shaped by abuse, bias, or harassment," then showing that PRO's own answer makes the platform the gatekeeper — "you cannot indict the gatekeeper and then hand him the gate." PRO's instrument-versus-proportionality distinction blunted but did not neutralize it.</best_rebuttal>
